issues.body: DischargeExpr::Other stores only left_operand, although an ODRL atomic constraint is the full (leftOperand, operator, rightOperand) triple. For Or(secx requirement, recipient == Bob), the returned tree cannot tell whether the non-proof branch holds because Bob and Eq were discarded; two recipient constraints with different values become identical. This also prevents correct XONE evaluation. That contradicts the API/docs claim that a host can read valid alternatives without returning to Policy. The test non_secprop_alternatives_are_kept_not_pruned is vacuous for this invariant because it asserts only the retained left operand.
issues.fix_hint: Preserve the complete non-secx Constraint in Other (for example, Other(Constraint), or explicit left_operand/operator/required fields), and add a test with two non-secx branches sharing a left operand but differing in operator/right value. Demonstrate that the returned tree alone distinguishes and evaluates the alternatives, including an XONE case, without consulting Policy.
issues.title: Other leaves still discard decision-critical constraint semantics

verdict.summary: Round 2 preserves AND/OR/XONE structure and fixes the prior flattening defect for secx leaves, but the advertised self-contained decision tree is still semantically incomplete. DischargeExpr::Other retains only left_operand and discards operator and right operand. Consequently a host cannot determine whether a non-secx alternative holds, distinguish two constraints over the same left operand, or evaluate XONE without consulting the original Policy. The new non-secprop alternative test checks only that the left operand survives, so it does not validate the documented claim that valid alternatives are readable from the result alone.
